C-COMMONMARK-EMPHASIS.IntentSummary: Emphasis delimiters pair the CommonMark way in both inline code paths. A new self-contained module scans `*`/`_` delimiter runs (escapes and code spans masked out), classifies flanking per CommonMark, and runs the delimiter-stack algorithm (nearest eligible opener, multiple-of-3 rule, consumption from the content side of runs) — returning the authoritative list of opener/closer segment pairs. Both existing emphasis dispatches (muya's WYSIWYG tokenizer and the marked fork used by HTML/PDF export and copy-as-HTML) consult it as a gate: a regex match is accepted only if the stack agrees with its opener and closer segments; when the stack pairs the current position's run with a different closer, a bounded match to exactly that closer is tried under the same validateEmphasize checks. Paragraphs without the ≥3-run theft shape take a zero-work fast path and stay byte-identical to today. The owner-report paragraph (`**Zero-shot **— … **One-shot**`) renders One-shot bold with the typo asterisks literal — on the editor AND in export — exactly as GitHub renders it.

MustContain.Text: const isValid = validateEmphasize(src, to[0].length, to[1], pending, validateRules)

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: src/muya/lib/parser/emphasisPairing.js exports computeEmphasisPairing(src) → null | { matches: [{openerSegStart, openerSegEnd, closerSegStart, closerSegEnd, type}] in document order } plus matchForSpan(start, end, markerLen) and matchForOpenerStart(pos) lookups. Run scan finds maximal `*`/`_` runs with CommonMark flanking (BOF/EOF = whitespace; PUNCTUATION_REG from ./utils; intraword-`_` restrictions). Escaped runs (odd preceding backslashes) and runs inside code spans (backtick-pair scanner) are masked. The delimiter-stack pass implements closers-left-to-right, nearest eligible same-char opener, odd-match rule ((closer.canOpen || opener.canClose) && closer.origLen % 3 !== 0 && (opener.origLen + closer.origLen) % 3 === 0 → skip), useDelims = both ≥ 2 ? 2 : 1, consumption from the content side of each run, leftover run length stays reusable, delimiters between a matched opener and closer are dropped from the stack, closers that find no opener and cannot open are dropped. Fast path: null (and no activation count) unless after masking some character has ≥ 3 runs with at least one can-open run followed by a later can-close run; when active, EMPHASIS_PAIRING_ACTIVATIONS increments once per computeEmphasisPairing call; resetEmphasisPairingActivations() exported for tests. MODULE_CONTRACT/MAP/CHANGE_SUMMARY from day one; ROLE RUNTIME, MAP_MODE EXPORTS.

parser/index.js strong|em dispatch: a per-invocation lazy memo computes computeEmphasisPairing(originSrc) on the first emphasis attempt. A regex match to[0] at absolute [pos, pos+len) with marker to[1] is emitted only when isValid (unchanged validateEmphasize) AND pairing.matchForSpan(pos, pos + to[0].length, to[1].length) — regex matches when pairing is null auto-pass. When the regex match is gate-rejected and pairing.matchForOpenerStart(pos) exists with markerLen = segLen, a bounded token raw=src.slice(0, closerSegEnd − pos) is emitted under the same checks (validateEmphasize with the bounded offset and marker, even trailing-backlash check applied to the bounded content, token shape identical to the regex path: type/marker/children/backlash/range) — children recurse with tokenizerFac exactly as the regex path does. On any failure the dispatch falls through to today's behavior (break to the chunks path / literal pending). Gate wrapped in START/END_BLOCK_EMPHASIS_PAIRING_GATE; MODULE_CONTRACT/LINKS/CHANGE_SUMMARY updated; no other dispatch branch touched.

marked/inlineLexer.js strong and em dispatches: output(src) captures the level's full src; offset = fullSrcLen − src.length; the pairing is memoized per output() level; the same two-step gate (matchForSpan for the regex match, bounded retry via matchForOpenerStart) wraps both dispatches after their existing validateEmphasize; lastChar/backlash handling unchanged; renderer calls unchanged. START/END_BLOCK_EMPHASIS_PAIRING_GATE marker; CHANGE_SUMMARY entry.

Correctness.Note: F1 (blocker, design): a naive gate "reject the regex match if any can-open run sits between opener and closer" is WRONG — the GitHub anchor for *foo **bar* baz** (triple-nested em) proves the mod-3 rule makes the intermediate ** ineligible there; muya currently gets that input right and the naive gate would regress it. Disposition: the full delimiter-stack algorithm (T-001) is required; no shortcut. F2: the regex and the stack consume delimiter runs at different edges for runs longer than the marker (***-class) — a single "does the stack agree" check would reject everything on *** inputs; disposition: the two-step gate (regex-aligned accept + bounded retry via matchForOpenerStart) with marker length taken from the stack segment. F3: bounded matches must keep the FULL validateEmphasize including lowerPriority — read of lowerPriority (parser/utils.js) shows it rejects only when a tighter construct CROSSES the candidate's edge (link-out-of-emphasis class *[foo*](bar) stays protected), while a code span fully inside survives; skipping it would regress rule-17. F4: delimiters inside code spans and behind escapes must never join the stack (GitHub anchor *a `*` b* → em with code inside) — masking added to T-001.

Security.Note: No new inputs, IPC, storage or network surface; the module is pure string analysis consumed by two existing parsers; no eval/regex-on-user-controlled-patterns beyond existing static rules.

UX.Note: User-visible effect is strictly the reported bug class: clean later pairs render as written (bold/italic), typo'd pairs show their asterisks the way GitHub shows them; no settings, no locales, no toolbar behavior change; the report paragraph renders identically in editor, HTML export, PDF print and copy-as-HTML.

Perf.Note: F5: running the pairing scan for every paragraph would tax exactly the C-LARGE-DOC-STAGE-0 territory (every keystroke re-tokenizes the active paragraph); disposition: the ≥3-runs-per-character fast path (R-2) with an activation counter pinned by tests, one linear pass with no backtracking when active, and memoization per string per dispatch level (children compute their own, by design). Tokenization cost for ordinary prose is unchanged (counter-pinned zero activations).

Correctness.Note: Post-implementation audit over the shipped code and gates. Live evidence: emphasis-pairing.test.js 9/9 (report paragraph → exactly one STRONG **One-shot** with the typo asterisks literal; marked byte-equals the GitHub API output for the report case; theft class, *** splitting em[strong], masking, round-trip, parity all pinned); muya suites 51 files / 643 tests green (634 pre-existing + 9 new); inline goldens re-captured through the C-24 UPDATE flow (UPDATE run fails by design, plain run green) with the diff limited to the three new STRESS entries; C-30 lexer goldens byte-unchanged. Two implementation corrections found and fixed during the pass, both recorded: (a) coordinate-space bug — tokenizerFac receives the parent's absolute pos, so the gate initially addressed the pairing with parent coordinates and produced a malformed nested EM on *foo **bar* baz** recursion; fixed with basePos (parser/index.js); (b) the *** improvement required extending the fast-path trigger to runs of length ≥3 (spec R-2 amended accordingly) and the marked bounded retry had to drop its per-dispatch type check (em-bounded was unreachable from the strong dispatch when the em regex does not match). Calibration: the activation counter semantics were re-pinned (single pair → 0, bold+italic four-run paragraph → 1, report → 1; plan C-9 corrected). Full-repository suite: 5000 passed, 20 failed — every failure proven pre-existing by an A/B run with all src/muya changes stashed (the same 20 fail without this change: editor-store.pending-opens 5, tabs-export 5, editor.test.ts 4, site gallery 3, export-docx 3 — parallel-session work, none touch emphasis); this bundle introduces zero new failures.

Security.Note: emphasisPairing.js is pure string analysis with two imports (PUNCTUATION_REG and nothing else at runtime beyond it); no dynamic regex construction from user input; both gates reuse the existing static rule tables; no IPC, storage, network or locale surface touched.
